title: Lathe Part (part-off) puts the blade centre on the part's end plane: a 3 mm blade cuts 1.5 mm into the finished part, and verify passes it

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: source:qa
labels.description: Found by the QA swarm (exploratory agent runs on real parts)

body:
Found by the QA swarm round 2 (#2582), brief q03 (turned pin, 70 mm long), CamCraft **v0.25.0** Linux x86_64 release, Tormach 15L Slant-PRO, post Tormach PathPilot Lathe. The G-code below was read by hand against the model.

## What happens

The part spans WCS Z 0 (front) to Z -70 (back face, with a 1 x 45° head chamfer at Z -70..-69); the bar runs on to Z -84. Op7_Part_Off: kind `part`, tool GT-0300 (3.0 mm wide grooving blade, orientation 2), `bottom_z` = bottom of model. Posted (q03-turn-shaft.nc lines 1813-1858):

```
(T0404 Parting_3mm - GROOVING BLADE ORIENTATION 2)
G0 X34
G0 Z-71.5
G1 X30 Z-71.5 F0.025
...
G1 X0 Z-71.5 F0.025
```

In the same program the groove finish passes show the convention since #641: the posted Z is the blade's -Z corner. The 2.5 mm O-ring groove Z -33.75..-36.25 is cut with the 2 mm blade at Z -36.25 and -35.75 (blade spans -36.25..-33.75, exact), and the 3 mm relief Z -17..-20 at Z -20 and -19. So the part-off blade at Z -71.5 spans **Z -71.5..-68.5**: it cuts 1.5 mm into the finished part's back face and removes the head chamfer. The part comes off 68.5 mm long instead of 70.

`verify` reports no warning for the operation (the lathe stock sim does not judge turning: "a turning program is cut by the field eye about its fitted spindle ... not judged here; the revolved verdict at generation stands"). The workaround the agent tried, `bottom_z` = bottom of model - 1.5, is refused: "nothing to part - the parting plane stands off the end of the bar" (the bar runs 14 mm further).

## Expected

The part-off blade's +Z flank stands at or behind the part's end plane (posted -Z corner at Z -73.0 for this 3 mm blade), or the operation is refused; a part-off that cuts into the part is a gouge and holds the post.

## Repro files

[q03-turn-shaft.camproj](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q03-turn-shaft/q03-turn-shaft.camproj), [q03-turn-shaft.step](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q03-turn-shaft/q03-turn-shaft.step), posted [q03-turn-shaft.nc](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q03-turn-shaft/q03-turn-shaft.nc) (lines 1610-1626 and 1716-1732 for the groove convention, 1813-1858 for the part-off); agent report [REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q03-turn-shaft/REPORT.md) problem 1.

Done means: on this project the part-off posts with the blade wholly at Z <= -70 (pinned by a generator test with a blade wider than zero, checking the blade's flank against the part end), and a parting pass whose blade overlaps the part is caught as a gouge before the post.
